records.summary_text:
[CW note] From the CryptoWeeklies video of 10 November 2026.

[2026-11-10_NVDA]  
Video Title: Nvidia Drops 20%: Can NVDA Hold Above $123 200-Week TWAP Support?  
Video ID: MJRMlux20Wg  
Nvidia (NVDA) | Class: EQUITY  

Current Market Structure  
• The AI‑sector remains in a deep accumulation zone, with NVDA and peers exhibiting 90 days of below‑median momentum and risk.  
• NVDA sits just above its 200‑week TWAP of $123, while the spot price is $166, indicating a 35% premium to the long‑term average.  
• The 20‑week SMA is near the 50‑week SMA, both hovering close to the 200‑week SMA, suggesting a consolidation phase rather than a breakout.  
• Momentum‑vs‑risk quadrant places NVDA in the “low risk, low momentum” corner, reinforcing its status as a value‑accumulation candidate rather than a high‑growth play.  

Quantitative Valuation & Gravity  
• The time‑weighted average price (TWAP) baseline for NVDA is $123, with a volume‑weighted average price (VWAP) of $52; the current price is 200% above VWAP, underscoring a strong gravity pull.  
• Gravity risk is quantified at 3 out of 10, placing the asset in the “moderate risk” band; historically, NVDA has spent minimal time at or below gravity level 3 since 2018.  
• The Efficient Frontier analysis shows NVDA offering a CAGR of roughly 25% over the past 90 days, but with a volatility that pushes it toward the upper edge of the frontier, implying a higher risk‑adjusted return.  
• Case study: In 2022, NVDA entered a “max despair” zone, fell to $37 (fair value), and rebounded to $166, illustrating a 3‑standard‑deviation capitulation that is now considered a rare event.  

Target Floors & Trap Identifications  
• Machine‑learning forecasts project a floor near the 200‑week TWAP of $123, with a 95% confidence band spanning $110–$140; a break below $110 would trigger a panic drawdown floor.  
• The standard‑deviation band analysis indicates that the current price is at the upper edge of the 3‑σ channel, suggesting a high probability of mean reversion toward the $123 baseline.  
• Value traps are identified around the 200‑week TWAP level; a sustained dip below $123 could lock in a 35% premium loss, while an overextension above $166 risks a rapid pullback.  
• Oracle (Oracle) serves as a comparative benchmark: its price of $118 is a 21% discount to its TWAP, with a gravity risk of 8 out of 100, highlighting NVDA’s higher gravity exposure and potential for a sharper rebound.
